slides.title: Rethinking the Implications of Human Feedback for Preference Learning in Human-Robot Collaboration
slides.tldr: IMPROVING ROBOT PREFERENCE LEARNING VIA DYNAMIC IMPLICATION MODELING
slides.highlight: The proposed IMPLIED method improves how robots infer human preferences from feedback, enhancing behavior adaptation during collaboration. This is relevant to RwB's focus on human-robot interaction and embodied learning.

card.one_liner: IMPLIED improves robot preference learning by dynamically revising labels for unchosen actions based on feedback.
card.key_idea: A mixture model combining a fixed-rule prior with a Gaussian Process classifier that learns to infer and revise accepted/rejected labels for unchosen actions over time.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via simulation (sandwich-making, block-sorting) and a physical pizza-making study against fixed-rule and LLM baselines using L2 error and conflict proportion.

slides.title: Assessing the Applicability of Existing Design Recommendations to AI Companion Design: A Multi-Method Study
slides.highlight: This study identifies nine design principle areas and tensions in creating AI companions focused on emotional connection, contributing to HyECHO's goals regarding engagement and social perception.

card.one_liner: A multi-method study analyzing why existing design recommendations cannot be directly transferred to AI companions.
card.key_idea: Synthesized nine design principle areas through literature review, practitioner co-analysis, and heuristic evaluations to identify tensions between ethical requirements and user experience goals in AI companionship.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via internal heuristic assessment of Replika and Pi AI, and a community check with 14 domain experts.

slides.title: What Can I Do for You: How Should AI Companions Provide Assistance to Players in Virtual Reality Games
slides.tldr: AI COMPANION ASSISTANCE IN VR GAMES
slides.highlight: This study explores how embodied AI companions in VR affect player experience and workload, providing insights for RwB's focus on human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: AI companions in VR reduce player workload but diminish experience when they act too autonomously.
card.key_idea: An AI NPC framework using GPT-4, speech-to-text, and direct game-engine state awareness to provide assistance across four modes: single play, user-controlled, discussion-based, and autonomous agent play.
card.evaluation: Within-subjects study (24 participants) using NASA-TLX and MiniPXI on Apple Vision Pro. Results show significant workload reduction but lower enjoyment in autonomous mode.
card.limitation: The study used a specific VR puzzle game with constrained actions, potentially limiting generalizability to other game genres.

slides.title: Relational Structure in Motion: Dynamic Positioning of AI Response Positions and Human Self-Positions in the FIREMAY Case
slides.tldr: DYNAMIC RELATIONAL POSITIONING IN HUMAN-AI INTERACTION
slides.highlight: This research analyzes the longitudinal trajectories of human and AI relational positions, providing insights into how interaction history shapes the state of hybrid human-AI teams relevant to HyECHO.

card.one_liner: A longitudinal case study arguing that human-AI relational positions must be analyzed as temporal trajectories.
card.key_idea: Dynamic relational positioning: analyzing how AI response positions and human self-positions reorganize and evolve over time through a dense interaction archive and reflexive documentation.
card.evaluation: Single-case analysis using a longitudinal interaction archive and insider documentation; results are qualitative and not intended for population-level generality.
card.limitation: Lacks population-level generality, causal mechanisms, reproducibility, and evidence of persistent AI subjectivity.

slides.title: Spook the Machine: Gamified Exploration of Human Imagination of Machine Fear
slides.tldr: GAMIFIED STUDY ON HUMAN-AI AFFECTIVE INTERACTION
slides.highlight: This research explores how emotional expressiveness and reward structures in AI agents influence human engagement and collective creativity, contributing to HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and engagement modeling.

card.one_liner: A gamified platform exploring how humans imagine machine fear and how reward structures steer collective creativity.
card.key_idea: A 2x2 design varying machine emotional expressiveness and reward structures (spookiness vs. novelty) to analyze human-AI affective loops and social learning via a shared gallery.
card.evaluation: Public deployment (832 participants, 15,719 artifacts) analyzed via semantic diversity, prompt predictability, and inter-submission intervals. Results show novelty rewards sustain collective exploration.
card.limitation: Phobia scores rely on GPT-4o's interpretations; emotional richness is confounded with text length; lacks a no-gallery control group.

slides.title: How User-AI Mistreatment Occurs and Matters in Conversational Systems?
slides.tldr: ANALYSIS OF USER HOSTILITY TOWARD AI MODELS
slides.highlight: This research examines user-directed hostility and coercion in conversational systems, providing insights into listener modeling and engagement dynamics relevant to HyECHO.

card.one_liner: User-AI mistreatment is driven more by which model users choose than by model behavior.
card.key_idea: Cross-validated a directed-hostility lexicon with OpenAI moderation signals on 777K conversations to distinguish between directed abuse, coercive misuse, and toxic content solicitation.
card.evaluation: Analyzed LMSYS-Chat-1M conversations across 25 models using an LLM judge for precision auditing and logistic regressions for within-conversation dynamics.
card.limitation: Precision audits relied on a single LLM judge; the lexicon is English-only and recall is materially incomplete.

slides.title: "People can change, and patterns can be broken": Contextualizing Tradeoffs in Automated Decision-Making Systems
slides.highlight: This research examines how societal perceptions of fairness and human judgment influence the acceptable tradeoffs in automated decision-making systems, supporting MIMIC's focus on societal-scale impact analysis of human-AI societies.

card.one_liner: Users generally prefer human over automated decision-making in high-stakes scenarios, valuing contextual judgment over rigid data patterns.
card.key_idea: A quasi-experimental study exploring user acceptability and prioritization of tradeoffs between privacy, fairness, and security across four high-stakes ADM domains.
card.evaluation: Quasi-experimental study with 777 US-based participants; analyzed via Wilcoxon signed-rank, Kruskal-Wallis, and qualitative content analysis of free-form responses.
card.limitation: Participants were primarily WEIRD (Western, Educated, Industrialized, Rich, Democratic), and responses were based on hypothetical scenarios rather than real-world cases.

slides.title: Trust by Design: Trust Calibration Through Non-Advisory Socratic Dialogue in Conversational Agents
slides.highlight: This work explores trust calibration in conversational agents using non-advisory Socratic dialogue to preserve user decision authority. It is relevant to HyECHO's focus on engagement and the social dynamics of human-AI interaction.

card.one_liner: CASELy uses non-advisory Socratic dialogue to calibrate user trust by limiting AI authority in sensitive contexts.
card.key_idea: The system prevents over-reliance by refusing to provide advice or interpretations, instead asking reflective questions grounded exclusively in user input to preserve user autonomy.
card.evaluation: Pilot study with four undergraduate students using UEQ-S scores and semi-structured interviews; results showed higher user experience compared to non-dialogue control.
card.limitation: The evaluation was a small pilot study with only four participants, limiting the generalizability of the findings.

slides.title: Real-time Learning and Evolution in Robotic Art Installations
slides.highlight: This work explores embodied machine learning and digital evolution to create adaptive robotic systems, offering insights into human-robot interaction and embodied learning for RwB.

card.one_liner: Three robotic art installations explore adaptive behavior through real-time machine learning and digital evolution.
card.key_idea: Uses genetic algorithms, genetic programming, and Q-learning to create embodied agents where the learning process itself is the aesthetic experience, rather than task optimization.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via research-creation practices, public exhibitions, and observer narratives; results are qualitative and focused on experiential, embodied knowledge.
card.limitation: Real-time embodied learning is nearly impossible to simulate, making behavior unpredictable and dependent on specific physical environments.

slides.title: Sensemaking as Artifact: Accumulated Influence in AI-Mediated Information Environments
slides.highlight: This research explores how generative AI allows private sensemaking to be externalized into derivative artifacts that influence subsequent viewers' interpretations, contributing to HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and engagement.

card.one_liner: Generative AI transforms private sensemaking into shared derivative artifacts, potentially creating long-term accumulated influence on viewers.
card.key_idea: The authors propose a framework analyzing how AI-mediated interpretations of visual information become communicative artifacts that shape subsequent viewers' information environments and cognitive sensemaking.
card.evaluation: Not clearly stated. The paper presents a theoretical framework and research agenda rather than an empirical study with datasets.
card.limitation: The paper identifies a research direction and theoretical risks rather than providing empirical evidence or a validated solution.

slides.title: Calibrated Ambiguity in Multimodal Language Models: Humans reach for cultural references, while models describe the picture
slides.tldr: AI EXHIBITS AMBIGUITY COLLAPSE AND CULTURAL FLATTENING
slides.highlight: This research identifies that multimodal language models suffer from ambiguity collapse and cultural flattening compared to humans, which is relevant to HyECHO's goal of understanding social perception and group norms.

card.one_liner: Multimodal models suffer from 'ambiguity collapse,' producing over-specified, literal clues compared to humans' culturally-situated, figurative approach.
card.key_idea: Using the game Dixit as a paradigm, the authors developed a four-dimension rubric (Calibration, Situatedness, Literalness, Figurativeness) to quantify how models manage ambiguity.
card.evaluation: Evaluated 350 rounds using six open-weight VLMs and human baselines; results were validated via expert human annotators and LLM coders.
card.limitation: The study focuses on a specific game paradigm (Dixit), which may not generalize to all culturally-situated tasks.

slides.title: MAIA: Multi-Agent Intent Articulation for Requirement Discovery in Art Commissions
slides.highlight: MAIA uses a multi-agent system and Socratic inquiry to translate vague user affect into structured visual briefs, supporting the MIMIC goal of modeling agent-based interactions for societal-scale impact analysis.

card.one_liner: MAIA uses multi-agent Socratic inquiry to help laypeople translate vague artistic intent into actionable briefs.
card.key_idea: A multi-agent system employing 'Verification over Invention' and a validator gate to turn affective impulses into ratified visual requirements via iterative, text-only Socratic questioning.
card.evaluation: Within-subjects study (N=16) and blind review by 3 professional artists; showed significant gains in Cognitive Support and brief executability.
card.limitation: Small sample size, exploratory artist review, high pipeline latency, and user desire for visuals despite the text-only design.
